quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Before every ride, you should check all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your motorcycle carefully. Check the rims and spokes for bends, looseness, or damage. Check your tire condition and tread. Check all lights.

questions.question: How can you increase the chance that other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight at intersections to be more visible. Position yourself in the lane where oncoming drivers can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can take quick action if needed.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When downshifting, move down one gear at a time. Slowly release the clutch through the friction zone between each shift.

questions.question: Your body can only get rid of alcohol through:
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. There is no faster way to become sober.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces are dangerous for motorcycles. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates reduce traction. Dry pavement is the safest.

questions.question: What is usually found in the center of a lane?
questions.explanation: Oil and grease from vehicles collect in the center of lanes. Motorcycles can usually ride safely on this strip when it is dry.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time. They are most effective when used together.

questions.question: Can clothing help protect you in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if garments are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: The right clothing reduces injury risk in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants made of sturdy material that completely cover your arms and legs. They should fit snugly and not flap in the wind.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, you should consider:

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which part of the lane will make your trip shorter.
If you can pass more vehicles in one position than another.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position has many benefits. Most importantly, choose a position where other drivers can see you and where you have enough space to take quick action if needed.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are used for traffic rules like speed limits. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose footwear with soles that:

options.text: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
Are made of soft, flimsy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
questions.explanation: Choose riding boots or shoes that are high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. The soles should be made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: To get the best protection, make sure your helmet:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no obvious defects.

questions.question: A horn:

options.text: Is not required on a motorcycle.
Should always be sounded when riding in fog.

questions.explanation: A street-legal motorcycle must have at least a headlight, taillight, brake light, front and rear brakes, turn signals, a horn, and two mirrors.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You do not need to check over your shoulder if you use your mirrors.
Mirrors provide a full view of the road around your motorcycle.
You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
You can assume drivers will respond correctly to your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Keep an adequate following distance behind other vehicles:

options.text: To give you time and space to spot and react to hazards.
To help traffic counters count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time and space to spot and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Keeping an adequate following distance gives you enough space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. This space also helps you see hazards on the road, like potholes.

questions.question: Which fabric provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the most protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if the pass can be completed before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: If you wait an hour per alcoholic drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.explanation: On average, a person's body can eliminate about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system and affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A good way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before.
Not assume they have experience and explain how to ride safely.
Not explain anything since they are only a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume they have experience and explain how to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Your passenger needs to know how to stay safe. Do not assume they have ridden before. Give them clear instructions before every ride.

questions.question: An advantage to keeping a riding group small is:

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic.
A small group can ignore traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always be trying to catch up.
It will be hard to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic.
questions.explanation: Small groups have several advantages. Other vehicles can pass them more safely. They are less likely to be separated by traffic or red lights. Slower riders do not have to rush to catch up.

questions.question: To get the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around your head and have no damage.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be ridden in curves.
Should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar turns and corners differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: How is the accelerator controlled?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.
